examples.problem: Find all of the solutions to $x^3-3x^2+12x-10 = 0$ given that $x=1+3\text{i}$ is a solution.
examples.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(x) = x^3-3x^2+12x-10.$ 

Since $f(x)$ has real coefficients and $x_1=1+3\text{i}$ is a root of $f(x),$ the complex conjugate 

$$
\overline{x_1}=\overline{1+3\textrm{i}}=1-3\text{i}
$$

must also be a root of $f(x).$

Now, according to the factor theorem, 
$\big(x-(1+3\text{i})\big)\big(x-(1-3\text{i})\big)$
is a factor of $f(x).$ Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-(1+3\text{i}))(x-(1-3\text{i})) & = \\ {x}^{2}-(1+3\text{i}+1-3\text{i})x+(1+3\text{i})(1-3\text{i}) & = \\ {x}^{2}-2x+({1}^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ {x}^{2}-2x+10 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the quotient when $f(x)$ is divided by $x^2 - 2x + 10$ using polynomial division.

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,\,x-1 \\  & {x}^{2}-2x+10\,\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+12x-10\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+10x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,-{x}^{2}+2x-10 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{\,-\,{x}^{2}+2x-10}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $f(x) = (x^2 - 2x + 10)(x-1).$ 

To find the remaining root, we set the linear factor equal to zero and solve for $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}x-1=0\,⟹\,x=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the roots are $x=1, 1 \pm 3\textrm{i}.$

feedback.problem: Given that $x=\frac{1}{3}$ is a solution to the equation $3{x}^{3}-7{x}^{2}+8x-2=0,$ find the remaining solutions.
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=9{x}^{3}-21{x}^{2}+24x-6.$ Since $x=\frac{1}{3}$ is a root of $f(x),$ then according to the factor theorem $(x-\frac{1}{3})$ is a factor of $f(x).$ 

We find the quotient when $f(x)$ is divided by $(x-\frac{1}{3})$ using synthetic division.

$$
\begin{aligned}\enclose{bottom right}{\frac{1}{3}} & 3 & -7 & 8 & -2 \\  &  & 1 & -2 & 2 \\  & 3 & -6 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $f(x)=(x-\frac{1}{3})(3{x}^{2}-6x+6).$ 

To find the remaining two roots, we solve $3{x}^{2}-6x+6=0$ by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-6x+6 & =0 \\ 3({x}^{2}-2x+2) & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-2x+2 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-2x+1+1 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2}+1 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =-1 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =(\text{i})^{2} \\ x-1 & =\pm \text{i} \\ x & =1\pm \text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions to our original equation are $x=\frac{1}{3},\,1\pm \text{i}.$
